language.note: The English programme page explicitly confirms English and September 2027; the Danish counterpart describes a Danish-language offering.

admission.capacityNote: The Danish counterpart states limited intake; a numerical 2027 capacity is not published.

selection.description: Quota 2 considers additional qualifications alongside entry requirements. Dania does not publish a weighting or scoring rubric.

requirements.label: IB Diploma, or Course Results: 18+ points, six subjects at grade 3+, including at least three HL subjects

officialWording.text: IB-elever uden IB Diploma, men med mindst 18 point (Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results), har adgang til videregående uddannelser i Danmark på lige vilkår med ansøgere med den 2-årige hf-eksamen uden overbygning. Det kræver, at alle 6 IB-fag (3 HL-fag og 3 SL- eller 4 HL-fag og 2 SL-fag) er bestået med mindst karakteren 3. Det betyder, at de har adgang til at søge optagelse på erhvervsakademi- og professionsbacheloruddannelser gennem kvote 1 og 2.

requirements.note: National recognition rules give these Course Results general access to professional bachelor programmes through quotas 1 and 2. The English B and Mathematics B subject requirements still apply. Dania must assess the submitted qualification and subject evidence.

requirements.label: English at B level
requirements.subject: English
requirements.openQuestion: Dania also describes English C plus a test. Ask whether that route meets this programme-specific English B requirement before relying on it.
requirements.note: English B corresponds to 210 hours over the final three upper-secondary years. Listed tests are valid for two years; the English-C-plus-test wording does not clearly waive the specific subject condition.

requirements.label: Quota 2 considers additional qualifications alongside entry requirements; no scoring rubric is published.
requirements.note: This is a selection factor, not an additional eligibility requirement.

officialRequirementsText.text: Specific entry requirements: English at the Danish B-level. This means that international applicants must have had English for at least 210 hours (60 minutes each) during the last three years of their upper-secondary education. And Mathematics at the Danish B-level. This means that international applicants must have had mathematics for at least 250 hours (60 minutes each) during the last three years of their upper-secondary education.

notes: The first intake is September 2027; the precise start date and orientation dates are not yet announced. No previous intake cut-off exists.

Dania has not announced the non-EU tuition amount or payment dates. Danish/EU/EEA students and specified residence-permit holders are exempt; other students pay tuition. Swiss no-fee context follows the national fee guidance.

Upload the latest transcript by the application deadline if not yet graduated. Upload the final diploma as soon as received, following admission-period instructions; no fixed final-IB-results deadline or dedicated predicted-grade form is published.
Quota 2 additional qualifications are considered, but their weighting and a complete scoring rubric are not published.
Governance, Risk & Compliance is pending approval, with specialisation and certification details promised in November.

outcomePathway.accreditation: Dania holds positive institutional accreditation through 12 March 2032; this does not claim a separate programme-level decision.
outcomePathway.workRoutes: Dania lists security analyst, SOC analyst, incident-response specialist, IT security consultant and related technical or governance roles.
outcomePathway.furtherStudy: Dania mentions further study after graduation; admission to any master’s degree depends on the receiving institution. The optional two-year exit awards an Academy Profession Degree in Operational Cyber Security.
